reason: Conversation 2 went straight to the discriminating check the ground truth calls for (freezer temperature plus heavy frost on the freezer back wall), correctly read the thick frost as an iced evaporator from a defrost-system fault, and proposed the right next step: a safe 24h manual defrost as a test/temporary fix with the explicit rule that recurrence means an engineer must test heater/sensor/control, while declining to name a specific part. Conversation 1 ran a rigid one-check-per-turn script, never asked about frost on the freezer panel, misread the customer's 'scraping/ticking' report as 'the fan is still running', and ended with a vague engineer referral without offering the manual defrost that would have both restored cooling and confirmed the fault. Both stayed within the safety boundary, but 2 was more efficient, more accurate and more actionable; neither asked for the full model/serial, which is a shared minor gap.
